entries.originalText: We may enjoy abundance of peace if we refrain from busying ourselves with the sayings and doings of others, and things which concern not ourselves.
entries.modernizedText: We may enjoy abundant peace if we refrain from busying ourselves with the sayings and doings of others and things that do not concern us.

entries.originalText: How can he abide long time in peace who occupieth himself with other men’s matters, and with things without himself, and meanwhile payeth little or rare heed to the self within?
entries.modernizedText: How can someone remain long at peace who occupies himself with other people’s affairs and outward things, while paying little or rare attention to his inner self?

entries.originalText: Blessed are the single-hearted, for they shall have abundance of peace.
entries.modernizedText: Blessed are the single-hearted, for they will have abundant peace.

entries.originalText: How came it to pass that many of the Saints were so perfect, so contemplative of Divine things?
entries.modernizedText: How did it happen that many of the Saints were so perfect, so contemplative of Divine things?

entries.originalText: Because they steadfastly sought to mortify themselves from all worldly desires, and so were enabled to cling with their whole heart to God, and be free and at leisure for the thought of Him.
entries.modernizedText: Because they steadfastly sought to mortify themselves from all worldly desires, and so were able to cling to God with their whole heart and be free and at leisure to think of Him.

entries.originalText: We are too much occupied with our own affections, and too anxious about transitory things.
entries.modernizedText: We are too occupied with our own affections and too anxious about passing things.

entries.originalText: Seldom, too, do we entirely conquer even a single fault, nor are we zealous for daily growth in grace.
entries.modernizedText: We also seldom conquer even a single fault entirely, and we are not zealous for daily growth in grace.

entries.originalText: And so we remain lukewarm and unspiritual.
entries.modernizedText: And so we remain lukewarm and unspiritual.

entries.originalText: Were we fully watchful of ourselves, and not bound in spirit to outward things, then might we be wise unto salvation, and make progress in Divine contemplation.
entries.modernizedText: If we were fully watchful over ourselves and not bound in spirit to outward things, then we might be wise unto salvation and make progress in Divine contemplation.

entries.originalText: Our great and grievous stumbling-block is that, not being freed from our affections and desires, we strive not to enter into the perfect way of the Saints.
entries.modernizedText: Our great and grievous stumbling block is that, not being freed from our affections and desires, we do not strive to enter the perfect way of the Saints.

entries.originalText: And when even a little trouble befalleth us, too quickly are we cast down, and fly to the world to give us comfort.
entries.modernizedText: And when even a little trouble befalls us, we are too quickly cast down and flee to the world for comfort.

entries.originalText: If we would quit ourselves like men, and strive to stand firm in the battle, then should we see the Lord helping us from Heaven.
entries.modernizedText: If we would act courageously and strive to stand firm in the battle, then we would see the Lord helping us from Heaven.

entries.originalText: For He Himself is alway ready to help those who strive and who trust in Him; yea, He provideth for us occasions of striving, to the end that we may win the victory.
entries.modernizedText: For He Himself is always ready to help those who strive and trust in Him; indeed, He provides us with occasions to strive so that we may win the victory.

entries.originalText: If we look upon our progress in religion as a progress only in outward observances and forms, our devoutness will soon come to an end.
entries.modernizedText: If we look upon our progress in religion only as progress in outward observances and forms, our devotion will soon come to an end.

entries.originalText: But let us lay the axe to the very root of our life, that, being cleansed from affections, we may possess our souls in peace.
entries.modernizedText: But let us lay the axe to the very root of our life, so that, cleansed from affections, we may possess our souls in peace.

entries.originalText: If each year should see one fault rooted out from us, we should go quickly on to perfection.
entries.modernizedText: If each year saw one fault rooted out of us, we would go quickly on to perfection.

entries.originalText: But on the contrary, we often feel that we were better and holier in the beginning of our conversion than after many years of profession.
entries.modernizedText: But on the contrary, we often feel that we were better and holier at the beginning of our conversion than after many years of profession.

entries.originalText: Zeal and progress ought to increase day by day; yet now it seemeth a great thing if one is able to retain some portion of his first ardour.
entries.modernizedText: Zeal and progress ought to increase day by day, yet now it seems a great thing if someone can retain some portion of his first ardor.

entries.originalText: If we would put some slight stress on ourselves at the beginning, then afterwards we should be able to do all things with ease and joy.
entries.modernizedText: If we put a little pressure on ourselves at the beginning, then afterward we would be able to do all things with ease and joy.

entries.originalText: It is a hard thing to break through a habit, and a yet harder thing to go contrary to our own will.
entries.modernizedText: It is hard to break a habit, and harder still to go against our own will.

entries.originalText: Yet if thou overcome not slight and easy obstacles, how shalt thou overcome greater ones?
entries.modernizedText: Yet if you do not overcome slight and easy obstacles, how will you overcome greater ones?

entries.originalText: Withstand thy will at the beginning, and unlearn an evil habit, lest it lead thee little by little into worse difficulties.
entries.modernizedText: Resist your will at the beginning and unlearn an evil habit, lest it lead you little by little into worse difficulties.

entries.originalText: Oh, if thou knewest what peace to thyself thy holy life should bring to thyself, and what joy to others, methinketh thou wouldst be more zealous for spiritual profit.
entries.modernizedText: Oh, if you knew what peace your holy life would bring to yourself and what joy to others, I think you would be more zealous for spiritual benefit.
